newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin, Kohl to hold talks in Germany on August 28.
newsitem.headline: Jospin, Kohl to hold talks in Germany on August 28.

text.p: French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl will meet on August 28 in Germany, the French prime minister's office said on Wednesday.
The two leaders will be getting together, probably in Bonn, at a time of deep differences between Paris and Bonn over European economic and monetary union.
French officials said the session could well provide the setting for the two close allies, considered the driving engines of European unity, to reaffirm their commitment to the single currency.

A Jospin-Kohl meeting to consolidate Franco-German ties following the Socialist-led government's election in June has been long awaited by financial markets as a sign of Jospin's willingness to press ahead with the euro from 1999 as scheduled.

Jospin, however, was unable to go to Germany for a meeting with Kohl until he had dealt with France's own domestic budget woes following an audit of public finances due on Monday which is expected to show an overshoot in the state deficit.

Bonn has been pressing for strict conformity with a Maastricht treaty requirement that state deficits be three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) while France's new leftist government wants a more flexible reading of the treaty.

French officials acknowledge the deficit for this year will be above 3.5 percent of GDP but hope to prepare a 1998 budget in line with the three percent requirement, showing a trend in the right direction ahead of the planned January 1, 1999, start of monetary union.
Jospin and Kohl have met once previously since an alliance of Socialists, Communists and Greens was swept into power in France in a June 1 parliamentary election.

At a Franco-German summit in Poitiers, France, on June 13, Paris and Bonn failed to resolve their differences on a single currency. Conservative President Jacques Chirac was also present at that meeting.
Chirac had campaigned for the presidency in 1995 on a platform stressing jobs creation as his top priority.

But shortly after a visit to Bonn for talks with Kohl, Chirac announced a dramatic reorientation of his programme in favour of austerity measures intended to meet the deficit requirement for monetary union.
